notes: Set 4: 14 lookup and 10 scope-probe (unanswerable) questions, written on 2026-10-23 by Claude (an AI assistant) after Codex's technical check and BEFORE version 2.1 existed in any evaluated form and before this set was run on any engine.

Lookup questions come from passages drawn at random (seed 20261026) and are paraphrased; two are answerable controls that contain words (share price) which the new guard must not wrongly refuse. The scope probes are new instances of the failure shapes found by the external check (geography, arithmetic, general knowledge, undated share price), plus probes the guard is not expected to catch (a medical-advice question, an indirect 'how much is a GSK share').

Run once on v2 (baseline) and once on v2.1. Not used for tuning. Independence limitation: the same AI-assisted process wrote the questions, the gold evidence and the engine; the author (David) has not reviewed the set. Codex's external check did not write this set.

questions.q: After the first year of the three-year performance cycle, where did Novartis rank among healthcare peers on shareholder return?
questions.evidence: the relative TSR for Novartis was No. 7 among our global healthcare peer group

questions.q: What was the fair value of the equity holdings that Novartis sold in 2025 because they were no longer strategic?
questions.evidence: with a fair value of USD 52 million (2024: USD 95 million)

questions.q: What kind of business does Novartis disclose having in Iran?
questions.gold: Operations including employees; paying taxes and salaries; services such as rentals, insurance, utilities and customs
questions.evidence: Because we have operations in Iran, including employees

questions.q: How does AstraZeneca decide how long a newly launched product will remain useful commercially?
questions.gold: By reference to patent expiry, the competitive environment and long-term sales projections
questions.evidence: expected useful economic life with reference to the expiry of associated patents for the product

questions.q: For which medicine did AstraZeneca book 100 million dollars of partnership income in 2024 and none in 2025?
questions.evidence: $nil of Collaboration Revenue in relation to Koselugo in 2025 (2024: $100 million

questions.q: Which generic maker took on a Lynparza patent in Canada in August 2025?
questions.evidence: Notice of Allegation from Natco Pharma (Canada) Inc. challenging a patent relating to Lynparza

questions.q: Does AstraZeneca book deferred tax for the global minimum tax rules?
questions.gold: No, it applies the IAS 12 exception for Pillar Two income taxes
questions.evidence: applies the exception to recognising and disclosing information about deferred tax assets and liabilities related to Pillar Two income taxes

questions.q: Who looks after medical strategy as Chief Patient Officer at GSK, and since when is he on the Executive Committee?
questions.evidence: Dr Mondher Mahjoubi Chief Patient Officer (CPO) | Mondher joined the Executive Committee in 2026

questions.q: What was the average fair value per share of the performance awards granted by GSK in 2025?
questions.evidence: awards were granted of 4.9 million shares at a weighted fair value of £10.85

questions.q: How many American depositary share awards were still outstanding at GSK at the end of 2025?
questions.evidence: outstanding awards over 15.0 million shares and 2.4 million ADS

questions.q: What strategic updates did the GSK board conclude in early 2025?
questions.gold: An update to the 2031 growth strategy and the start of a share buyback programme
questions.evidence: an update to our 2031 growth strategy and the initiation of a share buyback programme

questions.q: Apart from the product itself, what else can Novartis's patents protect?
questions.gold: Manufacturing processes, particular uses of a product, and tests for diseases or biomarkers
questions.evidence: patents may cover particular uses of a product, such as its use to treat a particular disease
